Allrighty :-)

Everything is a mixture of three things.

One of the basis is: I cut two apples into thin slices and sprinkle them with cinnamon. 2-4 minutes in the microwave oven, and you get something delicious, quick, and sugarless.

The almond and fruit cake is done like this:

Ingredients for the sponge cake:

1 orange OR one lemon OR two apples OR whatever fruit you want it to taste like.

6 eggs

100 grams (3,52 ounces) erythritol (I don't like the taste of this one much, so I only use this if I'm going to put something else on the cake: if I'm going to eat the cake on its own, then 1 tablespoon of xylitol and 1 tablespoon honey, they taste much better: you can choose whatever you prefer to sweeten it).

250 gr (8,81 ounces) almond flour (basically, raw almond in dust form, the grain doesn't need to be very small)

1 teaspoon baking powder

Butter

To-do: If you use one lemon or one orange, you have to put it in a bowl with water and cook it for 30 minutes. Then change the water, and cook for another 30 minutes (this is the longest step).

If you do it with a cinnamon sprinkled apple, four minutes in the microwave oven will have it ready.

  1. Preheat the oven at 190º C, 374º F

  2. Mix the eggs with the sweetener (whatever you're using, in my case erythritol). Add the almond and baking powder and mix.

  3. If you used lemon, orange or tangerine, cut them into pieces to take out any seeds that might have got there. Mash it (including the peel) and add it to the dough. The apple, again, can go straight there (supposedly it was pitted and sliced before it went inside the microwave).

  4. Spread butter on a mold. Pour the dough and bake 30 minutes, more or less (it's what takes in my oven). As with every baking thing, you have to pay attention to it. Maybe after 15 minutes it's a good idea (depending on the oven) to cover it with aluminum foil so the top doesn't get burnt. As always, to get to see if it's done, stick a knife into it: if it comes out clean, it's done. Otherwise, give it five more minutes.

This cake is the base I use for my fruit pies. After you have the cake (if you use apple it shouldn't take a lot of time), then there's the quick pie and the slow pie.

The quick pie I cut the cake into very thin slices (ideally, half a centimetre, which is about 0,20 inches), and cover the bases of about three molds (it allows for that much).

Slice two kilos (about four pounds) of apples, sprinkle them in cinnamon and put everything in a big pot with a glass of water (about a cup). Heat to medium until the apples become brown and soft. To be honest, I'm not sure I'm doing this one well, but I had to improvise because last time I did the four pounds apple by apple in the microwave oven, it took way too much. I will try this one next time (without the sugar, of course): http://www.goodtoknow.co.uk/recipes/176282/Stewed-apples

When you're done, you use the same liquid the apples left in the pot, to soak the cake (I am very much against dry cakes, but that's me, so you can skip this part). You cover the cake with the sliced apples (preferrably in a nice pattern, but that's not necessary), and then sprinkle them with some more cinnamon (I'm crazy for cinnamon, you will probably want to cut it short). In the end, you should have a very thin layer of cake and lots of apple. And in quantities that will last two weeks for two people.

The slow pie

First step is the same: cut the cake in very thin slices and cover the bottom of as many molds as possible.

The slow pie includes about two tablespoon of corn flour, but it's worth it. However, since I use European ingredients, I really recommend you to try your own experiments.

You will need 2 satches of caramel custard powder preparation (something like this: https://www.google.es/search?q=powder+pudding&client=firefox-b-ab&tbm=isch&tbo=u&source=univ&sa=X&ved=0ahUKEwjrw5WcsrPQAhXEbBoKHZvQDPoQsAQIGw&biw=1280&bih=679 I honestly don't know how this may work out of my country: you'll have to look for one that's sugarless, high quality, and as healthy as possible: normally it's refined corn flour with some flavouring), 2 litres of lactose-free milk, and whatever you use to sweeten (you can put less sweeteners if you want).

First, I make a more liquid pudding with a litre (4,22 cups) of lactose-free milk. I do the caramel custard following the instructions, replacing the sugar with one tablespoon xylitol and one tablespoon honey. With it, I soak the cakes (and then I sprinkle it with cinnamon). By the way, the amounts of sugar asked for these concoctions is insane.

Then, I do another batch of powdered caramel custard, only this one with half a litre (2,11 cups) of milk, 1 tbsp xylitol, 1 tbsp honey, and adding two eggs to the mixture. That creates a wonderful thick cream. I put it on top of the already soaked cakes (normally, it's not enough for all of them, but then some of the cakes don't have cream).

The cream cakes you can cover with cooked apples, but I prefer cranberries and raspberries.

If you add a bit of melted 0-sugar black chocolate on top of the cranberries or raspberries (just a few drops), that's a last nice details, but the cakes are great only with this.
